hero.name: Min Kim
hero.tagline: Hired as a product planner, became the company's first engineer
hero.description: Designed, built and shipped a B2B SaaS across web, iOS and Android as the sole developer in an organization with no engineering team. Worked on payments, auth, security and NFC in production, and took over stalled outsourced apps to bring them in-house.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: From planning to engineering
about.description1: I joined as a product planner, but with no engineers on staff my specs never got built. Building them myself turned out to be faster, so I did — and after shipping the product I moved into an engineering role.
about.description2: I now own the entire web service and the native apps. Subscription billing, multi-tenant security, native NFC integration and LLM-based document search were all built and debugged in a production environment with real paying customers.
about.description3: There was no engineering process in place, so I introduced one as needed — version control, database migrations, architecture documentation and security audits.

timeline.why: No way to roll changes back
Manual schema edits caused an incident
Hard to reason about my own older code

skills.title: Tech stack
skills.subtitle: Only what I have actually shipped and operated

items.title: TrayStorage Connect
items.summary: A B2B document management SaaS paired with NFC-tagged physical storage trays. I handled architecture, development, deployment and operations end to end.
highlights: Built subscription billing and migrated payment providers twice with no downtime for existing subscribers
Enforced multi-tenant isolation at the database level (118 row-level security policies)
Ran a self-directed security audit that surfaced object-storage credentials exposed in the frontend bundle
Natural-language document search on 18 LLM function-calling tools, migrated away from vector RAG
Five-language localization including full legal documents with scheduled revisions

items.title: Four native apps taken over and rebuilt
items.summary: Took over apps that had been outsourced and then left unmaintained for roughly 22 months. They were listed on the stores, but social sign-up was broken and most features were unimplemented.
highlights: Rebuilt four independent apps with separate bundle IDs (2 iOS, 2 Android)
Fixed Kakao, Naver and Google SDK integrations — sign-up was impossible before
Completed Android first, then brought iOS to parity against it
Analysed the codebase with no documentation and no original developer available, then weighed patching against a rewrite
Migrated the backend to Supabase and implemented OCR and AI chat functions

items.title: Native wrapper rebuilt from scratch
items.summary: An outsourced native wrapper stalled because NFC was never implemented, and the source code was never handed over. I rebuilt it from requirements alone, with nothing to reference.
highlights: NFC is structurally impossible through a web view alone — it requires a hand-written native bridge
Wrote four custom Capacitor plugins (NFC, push, speech-to-text, downloads)
Three-tier NFC intent filter so no tag type fails to register
Universal links and app links, plus App Store review guideline compliance
All code now owned in-house, removing the dependency on the vendor

personal.label: Personal project · open-source fork
personal.name: Desktop Pet World
personal.tagline: A real-time 3D world that runs on the desktop all day
personal.summary: A fork of the open-source desktop-pet app super-agent-party, with an entirely new 3D world layered on top. The render pipeline was redesigned around Apple Silicon thermals as a hard ceiling, and I built my own performance, regression and balance harnesses.
highlights: **Render pipeline redesigned under a thermal budget** — removed a post-processing chain (GTAO, bloom) that was stacking ~19 fullscreen passes per frame, replaced with a single forward pass plus MSAA. Idle-aware frame tiering at 60/30/15fps, all particles moved to shader Points, ocean waves moved to a vertex shader

**Three self-built verification harnesses** — a headless smoke test (including a draw-call ceiling assertion), an fps/CPU probe across idle states, and a Monte Carlo balance simulator that mirrors the pet decision logic over 400 virtual days

**Away-day simulation** — days you never connect are simulated from a date seed, written up as a diary entry from the pet's point of view, and folded into the world log. The pets bring it up next time you open the app
**Storage layer hardened after a real incident** — following data loss, the write path was rebuilt around atomic replace, generational backups, corruption quarantine and a three-step recovery ladder
**3D modelling** — both characters modelled in Blender; procedural textures and vertex-colour gradients mean no texture assets ship at all
personal.note: The repository is currently private. Happy to share code and screenshots on request.
